title: FullCD on a compactification gives the ambient exceptional adjoint
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an integer $n\geq1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$, using the valuation ring and chosen uniformizer of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] on which $\ell$ is invertible, let $X,Y$ be finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $S$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type $S$-morphism. Suppose a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ is given, with $j$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and suppose $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] for some integer $c\geq0$. On the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the chosen compact-support candidate $Rf_{!,n}:=Rp_*j_!$, with derived direct image as in [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and extension by zero as in [def-weil-extension-by-zero], preserves set-indexed coproducts and has a right adjoint $Rf_n^\times$. These adjunctions form an ambient exceptional right adjoint datum [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] with distinguished compactification $(j,p)$ and bound $c$: the adjunctions for compactifications are canonically identified along their compact-support comparison isomorphisms, with compatible units and counits and the cocycle condition for refinements.

source.place: sk-prop-sf-existence, clause (b), the conditional ambient pro-etale adjoint. The Brown step is Stacks Tag 0F5Y, injectives-proposition-brown; that tag alone does not assert the preceding pro-etale coproduct theorem. Related unfinished Lean: WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.ExceptionalAdjoint, lines 145-153, HasAmbientExceptionalRightAdjoint.isLeftAdjoint.

proof.text: Write $\mathsf M_T=\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] these are Grothendieck abelian categories, using the small-site universe fixed in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. By [lem-weil-proetale-module-direct-image-left-exact], $p_*$ is additive and left exact. The first clause of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] says $R^qp_*F=0$ for every sheaf $F$ and $q>c$; classical derived functors agree here with cohomology of the total derived image on a sheaf, by [lem-sp-kinjective-computes](2), applied to the finite-level construction [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. This uses sheaves on the entire source, not just those of etale origin. Properness makes $p$ qcqs. For every compactification $d=(j_d,p_d)$ the open $j_d$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], applied with base $Y$, source $X$ of finite type over $Y$, and separated target $\overline X_d\to Y$. The scheme $\overline X$ is finite type over $S$: $p$ is finite type by properness, and finite affine covers with finite lists of algebra generators compose with those for $Y\to S$. Thus the stated FullCD definition applies to this proper part.

proof.text: Use the existing [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] with the constant condensed ring $\underline A$ on profinite sets and complexes in degree zero. Its coefficient sheaf is exactly $A_T$: the functors $p_T^*$ in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] are geometric inverse images, so preserve copowers of the terminal sheaf, hence constant sheaves and their ring operations as defined in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Their composition comparisons identify $p^{-1}A_Y$ with $A_{\overline X}$. For a family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$, index by the filtered poset of finite subsets $J\subset I$, and set $K_J=(\bigoplus_{i\in J}M_i)[0]$. These complexes have common lower bound zero, and their termwise filtered colimit is $(\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i)[0]$, by the coproduct universal property. The cited continuity theorem gives $\varinjlim_J R^qp_*(\bigoplus_{i\in J}M_i)\cong R^qp_*(\bigoplus_iM_i)$, using the classical/total identification from step 1. The classical functors are additive: a finite sum of injective resolutions is an injective resolution of the finite sum, since finite biproducts of injectives are injective and finite sums are exact; applying the additive $p_*$ and taking cohomology preserves that finite biproduct. Thus the left side is $\bigoplus_i R^qp_*M_i$, with its canonical coprojections. This proves preservation of sums for every $q\geq0$, including $p_*=R^0p_*$. For injective sheaves $J_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing] now gives $R^qp_*(\bigoplus_iJ_i)=\bigoplus_i R^qp_*J_i=0$ for $q>0$: sums of injectives are $p_*$-acyclic. The empty family uses the same argument, since the finite-subset poset then has the single object $\varnothing$.

source.place: Clause (b), conditional ambient adjoint and compactification independence; expanded agent proof

proof.text: Given arbitrary unbounded complexes $(K_i)$, choose K-injective resolutions $K_i\to I_i$ with each term of $I_i$ injective, by [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence]. Their termwise sum represents the derived coproduct, by [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts]. Filtered-colimit exactness in the Grothendieck category makes direct sums exact (write a sum as the filtered union of finite sums); hence $\bigoplus_iK_i\to\bigoplus_iI_i$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Every term of $\bigoplus_iI_i$ is $p_*$-acyclic by step 2. Apply [lem-kun-finite-cd-acyclic-complex] with bound $c$ from step 1, both to each $I_i$ and to their sum. It identifies $Rp_*I_i$ with $p_*I_i$ and $Rp_*(\bigoplus_i I_i)$ with $p_*(\bigoplus_iI_i)$. The latter is termwise $\bigoplus_i p_*I_i$ by step 2. Naturality of the acyclic-complex comparison identifies these isomorphisms on every coprojection, so the map proved invertible is exactly $\bigoplus_i Rp_*K_i\to Rp_*(\bigoplus_iK_i)$. The same calculation covers the empty family.

source.place: Clause (b), conditional ambient adjoint and compactification independence; expanded agent proof

proof.text: By [prop-exc-open-adjoint], the derived $j_!$ is a left adjoint on all the ordinary derived categories. It preserves every coproduct: for any $L$, adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!(\bigoplus_iK_i),L)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus_iK_i,j^*L)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(K_i,j^*L)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(j_!K_i,L)$, with the indicated coprojections. Consequently $F_c=Rp_*j_!$ preserves all set-indexed coproducts by step 3. It is exact: the termwise $j_!$ is triangulated by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], and the unbounded $Rp_*$ is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Composing these shift and triangle identifications gives those for $F_c$.

source.place: Clause (b), conditional ambient adjoint and compactification independence; expanded agent proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-grothendieck-derived-brown-right-adjoint] to the Grothendieck category $\mathsf M_X$ and to the exact coproduct-preserving functor $F_c:D(\mathsf M_X)\to D(\mathsf M_Y)$ of step 4. It supplies a right adjoint $G_c$ and natural bijections $\Phi^c_{K,L}:\operatorname{Hom}(F_cK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,G_cL)$. Denote $G_c$ by $Rf_n^\times$. Brown is applied to the full unbounded source in a common indexing universe, without any compact-generation or constructibility premise.

source.place: Clause (b), conditional ambient adjoint and compactification independence; expanded agent proof

proof.text: For a refinement $u:d\to e$, put $V=\overline X_d\times_{\overline X_e}X$, with open $b:V\to\overline X_d$, projection $q:V\to X$, and section $s:X\to V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section], $s$ is a clopen section of $q$. Use the direct-image clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction] with the constant coefficient sheaf $A_{\overline X_e}$ and the site object $X\to\overline X_e$. The identification of geometric open restriction with localized restriction is [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. It gives the canonical natural isomorphism $j_e^*Ru_*N\cong Rq_*b^*N$ on all unbounded inputs. For $N=j_{d!}K$, the Cartesian square with sides $j_d,b,s,1_X$ gives $b^*j_{d!}K\cong s_!K$ by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change].

source.place: Clause (b), conditional ambient adjoint and compactification independence; expanded agent proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-clopen-section-component] to the clopen section $s$ of $q$. Choose a K-injective resolution $K\to J$ on $X$ by [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence]; the Grothendieck hypothesis is supplied by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. Exactness of $s_!$ [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] makes $s_!K\to s_!J$ a quasi-isomorphism. The component lemma makes $s_!J$ K-injective and gives the natural chain isomorphism $q_*s_!J\cong J$, by restriction to the $X$ component. Computation of total derived image on K-injectives [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] therefore gives $Rq_*s_!K\cong K$. Composing with step 6 gives $\lambda_u:j_e^*Ru_*j_{d!}K\cong K$, with exactly this component normalization. Naturality of the component chain isomorphism and derived comparison makes $\lambda_u$ natural in $K$.

source.place: Clause (b), conditional ambient adjoint and compactification independence; expanded agent proof

proof.text: By [lem-sp-proper-open-derived-support], the counit $j_{e!}j_e^*M\to M$, $M=Ru_*j_{d!}K$, is invertible; the quasi-compactness assumptions were checked in step 1. Define $\alpha_u:j_{e!}K\to Ru_*j_{d!}K$ as this counit after $j_{e!}(\lambda_u^{-1})$. It is a natural isomorphism. This is precisely where ambient proper support is needed: neither the etale-only comparison nor the bounded-below etale-origin comparison supplies this counit on arbitrary $K$. Also the presheaf defining $j_{e!}M$ in [def-weil-extension-by-zero], restricted to the localized site of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], is exactly $M$; it is already a sheaf there. Thus the open-adjunction unit $M\to j_e^*j_{e!}M$ is the identity identification, termwise and hence on derived categories. In combination with [prop-exc-open-adjoint] it gives $\operatorname{Hom}(j_{e!}K,j_{e!}L)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$, so extension is fully faithful. Maps between these supported objects are therefore determined by restriction to $X$.

source.place: Clause (b), conditional ambient adjoint and compactification independence; expanded agent proof

proof.text: For the identity refinement, $\alpha_1$ is the identity under the identity direct-image comparison, since its restriction is $1_K$. For composable refinements $u:d\to e$, $v:e\to h$, compare $\alpha_{vu}$ with $Rv_*(\alpha_u)\circ\alpha_v$, using the canonical $R(vu)_*\cong Rv_*Ru_*$ of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. They are equal: both source and target are supported on $j_hX$ by step 8 (the target identifies with $R(vu)_*j_{d!}K$), and restricting to $X$ gives the identity under $\lambda_{vu}$. To check that normalization, take a K-injective resolution on $\overline X_d$. Direct image preserves K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], applied to its exact inverse-image left adjoint in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and open restriction preserves them by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] under the site identification [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Thus the successive direct images and restrictions are computed on this common model: every open restriction is literal restriction of sections, the component $X$ is the same component in the iterated fibre product, and both composites there are $1_K$; the associativity normalization of the cited composition isomorphism identifies the two models. Thus, writing the composition comparison implicitly, $\lambda_{vu}\circ j_h^*(Rv_*\alpha_u\circ\alpha_v)=1_K=\lambda_{vu}\circ j_h^*\alpha_{vu}$; here naturality of restriction on sections gives the first equality. Full faithfulness from step 8 gives equality before restriction. Thus the proper/open comparisons satisfy identity and composition equations, as actual maps rather than merely unspecified isomorphisms.

source.place: Clause (b), conditional ambient adjoint and compactification independence; expanded agent proof

proof.text: For $u:d\to e$, proper composition and step 8 give $F_d=R(p_d)_*j_{d!}\cong R(p_e)_*Ru_*j_{d!}\xrightarrow{R(p_e)_*\alpha_u^{-1}}R(p_e)_*j_{e!}=F_e$; call the composite $\theta_u$. By [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] and step 9, $\theta_1=1$ and $\theta_{vu}=\theta_v\theta_u$. The category of compactifications is cofiltered by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered], applicable because $f$ is separated finite type, has the given compactification, and its open is quasi-compact by step 1. Hence for any $d,e$ choose a common refinement $r$ with arrows $a:r\to d$, $b:r\to e$ and set $\theta_{d,e}=\theta_b\theta_a^{-1}$. For two such choices, choose a further common refinement and then equalize the two resulting parallel arrows to $d$ and to $e$; functoriality of the $\theta_u$ makes the two expressions equal after cancelling the invertible maps from that further refinement. Thus the comparison is independent of the choice. For three objects, compute through one common refinement and cancel the map to the middle object: $\theta_{e,h}\theta_{d,e}=\theta_{d,h}$. These comparisons agree with those of individual refinements.

source.place: Clause (b), conditional ambient adjoint and compactification independence; expanded agent proof

proof.text: Fix the chosen compactification, denoted $c$ in the following comparison formulas (distinct from the integer bound), and abbreviate $t_d=\theta_{d,c}:F_d\cong F_c$, so $t_c=1$ and $t_d=t_e\theta_u$ for $u:d\to e$. Define $G_d=G_c$ for every $d$, and $\Phi^d(h)=\Phi^c(h\circ t_{d,K}^{-1})$. These are natural bijections, hence give adjunctions by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Their units and counits are explicitly $\eta^d_K=G_c(t_{d,K}^{-1})\eta^c_K$ and $\varepsilon^d_L=\varepsilon^c_L\,t_{d,G_cL}$. Set every right-adjoint comparison $\rho_u:G_e\to G_d$ equal to $1_{G_c}$. From $t_d=t_e\theta_u$ we get $t_e^{-1}=\theta_u t_d^{-1}$, hence $\eta^e_K=G_c(\theta_{u,K})\eta^d_K$ and $\varepsilon^d_L=\varepsilon^e_L\theta_{u,G_cL}$. These are exactly the two compatibility equations in [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], with $\rho_u=1$. Identity and composite comparisons for the right adjoints are identities, while those for the left adjoints were checked in step 10. Together with the given integer $c$ and its FullCD condition, this constructs every component of the stated ambient datum.

tool_uses.why: Step 1: all constant-ring module categories are Grothendieck; a generic ringed-site tool, with no replacement in the existence unit.
Step 1: additivity and left exactness of the ordinary module direct image; a functor-construction tool.

Step 2: bounded-below filtered continuity for a qcqs morphism, specialized to the constant condensed finite ring and degree-zero finite partial sums; this supplies continuity, not an exceptional adjoint or comparison theorem.
Step 2: geometric coefficient pullback identifies the constant condensed finite ring with the constant ring sheaf, coherently under scheme maps.
Step 3: termwise sums represent coproducts in the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck category; generic homological algebra.
Step 3: finite cohomological dimension makes an arbitrary complex of acyclic terms compute the total derived image; generic homological algebra using the stated FullCD bound.
Steps 4 and 7: exactness of the open extension functor; a sheaf operation tool.
Step 5: Brown for an exact coproduct-preserving functor from a Grothendieck derived category; precisely the existence route, not a substituted geometric theorem.
Step 6: the section in the proper/open fibre product is clopen; an elementary geometric tool independent of cohomological comparison.
Steps 6, 8 and 9: identifies open restriction with localization of the pro-etale site and fixes its section calculation.
Step 7: computation of a total derived functor on K-injective resolutions; generic homological algebra.
Step 6: Cartesian open-extension comparison for arbitrary complexes, applied to the square with top identity and lower map b; no proper base-change theorem is used.
Steps 9 and 10: ordinary finite-level unbounded direct-image composition, including identity and associativity, for constructing coherent refinement comparisons.
Step 10: cofilteredness for already supplied compactifications over an arbitrary base, used only to remove the choice of common refinement.

Step 6 uses only its generic unbounded ringed-site direct-image localization clause, specialized to constant finite coefficients and an open site object; no smooth-purity existence-unit node states this comparison.

Steps 4 and 8: the derived open adjunction j_! -| j^* on the full ordinary pro-etale derived categories, used for coproduct preservation of j_! and full faithfulness of j_{e!}; a generic sheaf-operation tool, no existence-unit node states it.
Step 9: termwise restriction of a K-injective complex to a localized site stays K-injective; generic homological algebra on ringed sites.
